purpose: Natalizumab-sztn is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) to help reduce the number of flare-ups and slow down disability. It is also used to treat moderate to severe Crohn's disease in people who have not responded well to other treatments. This medicine helps keep your condition more stable and improves your quality of life.
how_it_works: Your immune system sometimes sends harmful cells into your brain, spinal cord, or gut that cause inflammation and damage. Natalizumab-sztn works like a blocking agent — it attaches to certain proteins on those immune cells and stops them from crossing into those sensitive areas. Think of it as putting a 'Do Not Enter' sign on the doorway those harmful cells would normally use.
common_side_effects: Headache, tiredness, joint pain, nausea, stomach discomfort, urinary tract or lung infections, skin rash, and feeling depressed. Some people also notice dizziness or muscle aches after their infusion.
warnings: There is a serious risk of a rare but dangerous brain infection called PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy), caused by the JC virus. Because of this risk, this medication is only available through a special safety program called TOUCH. Tell your doctor right away if you notice new or worsening confusion, vision changes, weakness, or problems with balance. This medicine can also lower your ability to fight infections, so avoid contact with sick people and report any signs of infection promptly.
typical_dosing: This medication is given as an IV infusion (through a vein) in a clinic or infusion center, typically once every 4 weeks. Each infusion takes about 1 hour. You will be monitored during and after your infusion for any reactions.
